architecture.overview: DataHub employs a distributed, event-driven architecture based on Generalized Metadata Architecture (GMA) principles. It uses stream-based real-time processing with schema-first metadata modeling.
design_principles: Schema-first metadata modeling using Pegasus Data Language (PDL)
Stream-based real-time metadata processing (changes propagate within seconds)
Federated metadata serving (distributed ownership, centralized discovery)
Multi-technology backend strategy (optimized storage per use case)

data_flow: 1. Metadata ingestion via Python connectors or push APIs
2. Metadata Change Proposals (MCP) sent to GMS via Rest.li
3. GMS validates and writes to primary storage (MySQL/Postgres)
4. GMS emits Metadata Change Log (MCL) events to Kafka
5. MAE Consumer processes MCLs and updates Elasticsearch + Neo4j
6. Platform Events trigger Actions framework for automation
7. Frontend queries via GraphQL for display
8. Users interact with metadata through web UI
scalability_features: Federated metadata services for distributed teams (data mesh support)
Kafka-based event streaming for async processing
Configurable consumer groups for parallel processing
Graph database for efficient relationship traversal

modeling_language.description: LinkedIn's schema definition language, similar to Protocol Buffers or Avro IDL
modeling_language.serialization: Serialization-agnostic, converts to Avro for Kafka and JSON for REST APIs
modeling_language.validation: Strong typing from client to storage layer

entities.definition: Primary nodes in the metadata graph representing concrete items like datasets, users, dashboards, etc.
entities.registry: Entity Registry (entity-registry.yml) catalogs all entities and their associated aspects

aspects.definition: Smallest atomic units for writing metadata - collections of related attributes describing a specific facet of an entity
characteristics: Immutable by design (changes create new versions)
Stored as JSON blobs in primary storage

versioned_aspects.description: Carry numeric versions, stored in relational databases
versioned_aspects.versioning: Each field change creates new version with history

timeseries_aspects.storage: Elasticsearch and Kafka only (not in primary DB)
timeseries_aspects.features: Aggregatable via @TimeseriesField annotations for SQL-like group-by

benefits: Independent versioning - track changes per aspect type
Flexibility - aspects can vary greatly in complexity

relationships.definition: Named associations between exactly two entities (source and destination), forming edges in the metadata graph
relationships.implementation: Typically modeled as foreign key fields within aspects (URNs pointing to other entities)
relationships.directionality: Directed edges with naming reflecting direction (e.g., HasMember vs IsMemberOf)
relationships.bidirectional_queries: Graph databases enable efficient traversal in both directions regardless of storage direction
examples: ProducedBy - data lineage from job to dataset
Consumes - data lineage from job to dataset
features: Entity-neutral design (same relationship type across different entities)
Embedded in aspects as URN arrays or single URN fields
Automatically indexed in Neo4j for graph queries
Support complex queries like 'all owners of this dataset'

conclusion.final_assessment: DataHub is a production-ready, enterprise-grade data catalog and lineage platform with excellent metadata modeling patterns. The Apache 2.0 license allows free reuse. Its aspect-oriented metadata model, event-driven architecture, and multi-granularity lineage tracking are particularly noteworthy design patterns. However, the operational complexity is high, and the learning curve is steep due to LinkedIn-specific technologies (PDL, Rest.li). Best suited for large organizations with complex data ecosystems and dedicated platform teams. For smaller teams or simpler use cases, consider lighter alternatives or the managed DataHub Cloud service.
